From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Minesweeper of the Royal Navy

For other ships with the same name, see [HMS Sharpshooter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter "HMS Sharpshooter").

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/HMS_Sharpshooter_1938_IWM_FL_18955.jpg/330px-HMS_Sharpshooter_1938_IWM_FL_18955.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HMS_Sharpshooter_1938_IWM_FL_18955.jpg)

History

![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Naval_ensign_of_the_United_Kingdom.svg/60px-Naval_ensign_of_the_United_Kingdom.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)United Kingdom

Builder[HMNB Devonport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMNB_Devonport "HMNB Devonport")

Commissioned 17 December 1937
Fate Scrapped in November 1965

General characteristics
Class & type[_Halcyon_-class minesweeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halcyon-class_minesweeper "Halcyon-class minesweeper")
Displacement*   815–835 long tons (828–848 t)
*   1,310–1,372 long tons (1,331–1,394 t), full load
Length 245 ft 3 in (74.75 m)
Beam 33 ft 6 in (10.21 m)

Propulsion Steam turbines, 1750 shp
Speed 17 knots (31 km/h)
Range 7,200 nmi (13,330 km) at 10 knots (19 km/h)
Complement 80
Armament*   2 × [QF 4 in Mk.V (L/45 102 mm) guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QF_4_inch_Mk_V_naval_gun "QF 4 inch Mk V naval gun"), single mounts HA Mk.III
*   4 × [QF 0.5 in Mk.III (12.7 mm) Vickers machine guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vickers_machine_gun "Vickers machine gun"), quad mount HA Mk.I

**HMS _Sharpshooter_** was a [_Halcyon_-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halcyon-class_minesweeper "Halcyon-class minesweeper")[minesweeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minesweeper "Minesweeper") of the British [Royal Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Navy "Royal Navy"). Built at [Devonport Dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMNB_Devonport "HMNB Devonport"), _Sharpshooter_ was completed in 1937. She served through the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"), acting both in her designed role as minesweeper and as a convoy escort, escorting several [Arctic convoys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arctic_convoy "Arctic convoy"). She took part in the [evacuation from Dunkirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evacuation_from_Dunkirk "Evacuation from Dunkirk") in 1940, and sank the [German submarine _U-655_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-655 "German submarine U-655") in 1942.

Post war, she was converted to a [survey ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Survey_ship "Survey ship"), and was renamed **HMS _Shackleton_** in 1953. She was laid up into reserve in 1961 and sold for scrap in 1965.

## Design

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Design")]

The _Halcyon_ class were a class of dedicated [minesweepers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minesweeper "Minesweeper"), designed to be smaller and cheaper than the dual-purpose (minesweeping and colonial patrol vessel) minesweeping [sloops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sloop-of-war "Sloop-of-war") that had been built since the late 1920s (i.e. the [_Bridgewater_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgewater-class_sloop "Bridgewater-class sloop"), [_Hastings_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings-class_sloop "Hastings-class sloop") and [_Shoreham_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoreham-class_sloop "Shoreham-class sloop")), which as their design evolved, were becoming increasingly focused on escort duties and becoming too large for use as minesweepers.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-sloops_p13-2)

_Sharpshooter_ was 245 feet 6 inches (74.83 m)[long overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Length_overall "Length overall") and 230 feet 0 inches (70.10 m)[between perpendiculars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Length_between_perpendiculars "Length between perpendiculars"), with a [beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beam_(nautical) "Beam (nautical)") of 33 feet 6 inches (10.21 m) and a [draught](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_(hull) "Draft (hull)") of 10 feet 3 inches (3.12 m) at deep load.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4)[Displacement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Displacement_(ship) "Displacement (ship)") was 835 long tons (848 t) standard[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4) and 1,330 long tons (1,350 t) deep load.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3) Two [Admiralty 3-drum water-tube boilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-drum_boiler#Admiralty_boiler "Three-drum boiler") supplied steam to geared [steam turbines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_turbine "Steam turbine") driving two shafts. The machinery was rated at 1,750 [shaft horsepower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsepower#Shaft_horsepower "Horsepower") (1,300 kW) giving a speed of 17 [knots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knot_(unit) "Knot (unit)") (20 mph; 31 km/h).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3)

Armament consisted of two [QF 4 inch (102 mm) Mk V guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QF_4_inch_Mk_V_naval_gun "QF 4 inch Mk V naval gun") on High-Angle mounts and so capable of being used for [anti-aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-aircraft_warfare "Anti-aircraft warfare") duties,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3) with a close-in armament of one quadruple [Vickers .50 machine gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vickers_.50_machine_gun "Vickers .50 machine gun") mount.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4) One of the 4-inch guns was removed during the Second World War, while the multiple machine guns were replaced by 4–8 [Oerlikon 20 mm cannon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oerlikon_20_mm_cannon "Oerlikon 20 mm cannon"). Up to 40 [depth charges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_charge "Depth charge") could be carried when used in the escort role.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-4-5) The ship had a crew of 80 officers and other ranks.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4)

## Construction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Construction")]

_Sharpshooter_ was ordered on 2 March 1936 under the 1935 shipbuilding programme and was [laid down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keel_laying "Keel laying") at [Devonport Naval Dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMNB_Devonport "HMNB Devonport") on 8 June 1936.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_sharp-7) She was [launched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceremonial_ship_launching "Ceremonial ship launching") on 10 December 1936 and completed on 17 December 1937.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-jfs62p281-8)

## Service

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Service")]

Following commissioning (where she received the [pennant number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennant_number "Pennant number") N68[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4) - this was changed to J68 in 1940[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-9)) _Sharpshooter_ joined the 1st Minesweeping Flotilla based at [Portland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_harbour "Portland harbour"). Along with the rest of her Flotilla, _Sharpshooter_ moved to [Scapa Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scapa_Flow "Scapa Flow"), the Flotilla's war station, from August to September 1938 during the [Munich crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich_crisis "Munich crisis").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6) With other ships of the flotilla she took part in the search in June 1939 for the submarine [Thetis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Thetis_(N25) "HMS Thetis (N25)") which had sunk in Liverpool Bay. She then operated with the flotilla in the Channel, and took part in the Royal Inspection (Reserve Fleet Review) at Portland on 9 August 1939.

### Second World War

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Second World War")]

_Sharpshooter_ was still a member of the 1st Minesweeping Flotilla in September 1939, at the outbreak of the Second World War.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-10)

The outbreak of war saw _Sharpshooter_ clearing channels through minefields around Scapa Flow and off [Loch Ewe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loch_Ewe "Loch Ewe") and the [Clyde estuary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clyde_estuary "Clyde estuary").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1939-11) At the end of May 1940, the [British Expeditionary Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Expeditionary_Force_(World_War_II) "British Expeditionary Force (World War II)") (BEF) was trapped by German forces at [Dunkirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunkirk "Dunkirk"), France and it was decided to launch [Operation Dynamo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Dynamo "Operation Dynamo"), the evacuation of the BEF from Dunkirk. _Sharpshooter_ was one of the ships assigned to the evacuation.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-Rowp21-12) She made her first evacuation run on the morning of 29 May, landing 69 troops picked up from the Dunkirk beaches at [Dover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dover "Dover"), with a second run made on the morning of the 30 May, picking up 273 troops.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-BEFp98-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1940-14)_Sharpshooter_ was outbound on another run when at 22:10 hr, she collided with the Dover-bound steamer [_St Helier_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TSS_St_Helier "TSS St Helier"). _Sharpshooter_'s [bow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bow_(watercraft) "Bow (watercraft)") was badly damaged, and she was towed back to Dover by the [tugboat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tugboat "Tugboat")_Foremost 22_, the journey taking 11 hours.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-BEFp21,5-15) She was under repair at [Sheerness dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheerness_dockyard "Sheerness dockyard") and [Leith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leith "Leith") until September 1940, the opportunity being taken to fit _Sharpshooter_ with equipment for sweeping magnetic mines.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1940-14)

On 20 February 1941 _Sharpshooter_ was approaching [Harwich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harwich "Harwich") with sister ships [_Bramble_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Bramble_(J11) "HMS Bramble (J11)"), [_Britomart_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Britomart_(J22) "HMS Britomart (J22)"), [_Seagull_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Seagull_(J85) "HMS Seagull (J85)") and [_Speedy_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Speedy_(J17) "HMS Speedy (J17)") when they came under attack by two German aircraft. _Bramble_ was hit by a German bomb that failed to explode, but damage was minimal.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-damp300-16) From April, _Sharpshooter_ began to be used to escort convoys in the [Western Approaches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Approaches "Western Approaches").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1941-17)

#### Arctic convoys

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Arctic convoys")]

On 27 November 1941 she set out from [Hvalfjord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hvalfjord "Hvalfjord") in [Iceland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iceland "Iceland") as part of the escort of the [Arctic convoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arctic_convoys_of_World_War_II "Arctic convoys of World War II")[PQ 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_5 "Convoy PQ 5") to [Archangel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkhangelsk "Arkhangelsk") in the Soviet Union.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-rugp23-18)_Sharpshooter_ remained in Russia, minesweeping and providing local escort for Arctic convoys as they arrived and left Russian ports.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6) Convoys escorted included [PQ 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_8 "Convoy PQ 8"), [PQ 9/10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_9/10 "Convoy PQ 9/10"), [QP 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_QP_7 "Convoy QP 7") and [QP 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_QP_9 "Convoy QP 9").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-rug_p25-7,_30-1-19) On the night of 17/18 January 1942, _Sharpshooter_ had just joined the escort of PQ 8 when the German submarine [_U-454_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-454 "German submarine U-454") torpedoed and sank the destroyer [_Matabele_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Matabele "HMS Matabele"). _Sharpshooter_ helped to rescue survivors from _Matebele_ then launched a counterattack against the submarine.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1942-20)

At about 8.25 pm on the evening of 24 March 1942[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-21) while escorting QP 9 [[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBuschR%C3%B6ll199945%E2%80%9346-22) the leading gunner on the forward four-inch gun of _Sharpshooter_ spotted [German submarine U-655](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-655 "German submarine U-655") on the surface beam on, about two to three cables (370 to 556 meters) away and about 10 degrees off the minesweeper's starboard bow, with no crew apparently manning the conning tower or deck. Upon being called by the officer of the watch the captain Lieutenant-Commander David Lampen immediately called for emergency full ahead and called 'Stand by to ram'. ‘’Sharpsweeper’’ had just begun to gather speed when she struck the submarine just behind the conning tower.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-Paterson-23) The submarine turned rolled over due to the impact and bumped along the minesweeper's port side sinking as it disappeared astern and sank stern first south-east of Bear Island, in approximate position 73.00N, 21.00E.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-24) No trace of the submarine or her crew of 45 was found except for two lifebuoys and what may have been a canvas dinghy.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-Paterson-23) The bow of _Sharpshooter_ was badly damaged by the collusion. After shoring up the forward mess deck, she continued at slow speed to Iceland independent of the convoy, and from there to Leith for repair.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1942-20)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-blairp549-25) She was under repair until June 1942.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)

In September 1942, _Sharpshooter_ formed part of the close escort for the Arctic convoy [PQ 18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_18 "Convoy PQ 18"), with _Sharpshooter_ being used as a rescue ship to pick survivors from sunken ships as well as for more conventional escort duties.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-rugp42-44-26)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1942-20) The convoy came under heavy air and submarine attack, with 13 ships in total being sunk. _Sharpshooter_ rescued 101 survivors during the operation.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-Rowp163-27) In November 1942, _Sharpshooter_ escorted the return convoy [QP 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_QP_15 "Convoy QP 15") to Iceland, but on 27 November, shortly after leaving the convoy, collided with the cargo ship _Empire Snow_, badly damaging the minesweeper.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-rugp46-7-28)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1942-20)

#### Mediterranean

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Mediterranean")]

In April 1943 _Sharpshooter_ was ordered to join the 12th Minesweeping Squadron in the Mediterranean, and in July the year took part in [Operation Husky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Husky "Operation Husky"), the Allied invasion of [Sicily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sicily "Sicily").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1943-29) After Husky, _Sharpshooter_ continued to carry out minesweeping and convoy escort operations in the Mediterranean until October 1944 when she returned to home waters.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1944-30)

### Survey ship

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Survey ship")]

In May 1945, _Sharpshooter_ began conversion to a survey ship at [Chatham Dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatham_Dockyard "Chatham Dockyard"). Her armament was removed during this conversion, which continued until March 1946. On 3 April 1946, _Sharpshooter_ was damaged in a collision with the merchant ship MV _Fealtie_. After repair and working up, she was deployed to [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore "Singapore"), carrying out survey operations off [Malaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malay_Peninsula "Malay Peninsula") and [Borneo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borneo "Borneo").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-post-32) During surveys of [Penang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penang "Penang"), she discovered five submerged wrecks.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-33) On 13 October 1947 she collided with the merchant ship MV _Celebes_ and after repair continued survey duties before returning to Britain at the start of 1948. After refit she recommissioned, receiving the new pennant number A310, and operating out of [Lowestoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lowestoft "Lowestoft").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31)

On 15 June 1953 she took part in the Coronation [Fleet Review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleet_Review "Fleet Review") at [Spithead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spithead "Spithead"), and on 1 July that year was renamed _Shackleton_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-post-32)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31) She ran aground in the [Bristol Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol_Channel "Bristol Channel") on 28 October 1958, damaging her sonar dome.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31) On 20 August 1959, the prototype [Handley Page Victor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handley_Page_Victor "Handley Page Victor") B2 bomber crashed into the [Irish Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Sea "Irish Sea"). A large scale salvage effort was launched by the Royal Navy to locate and recover the wreckage, so the cause of the accident could be determined.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-34)_Shackleton_ was diverted from her normal survey duties to take part in this search and salvage operation,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6) and on 20 April, while searching for debris of the bomber, was diverted to the aid of a trawler, the _Starbank_, that had an uncontrolled leak. _Shackleton_ transferred pumps over to the trawler, which allowed the leak to be controlled, and escorted _Starbank_ to [Milford Haven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milford_Haven "Milford Haven").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-35)

### Disposal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Disposal")]

_Sharpshooter_ was refitted at Devonport in 1961, but was then immediately paid off into reserve. She was placed on the disposal list in 1965 and was sold to the [British Iron & Steel Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Iron_&_Steel_Corporation "British Iron & Steel Corporation") (BISCO) for scrapping. The ship was allocated to the West of Scotland Shipbreaking Company, and arrived at their [Troon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troon "Troon") yard for breaking up on 3 November 1965.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31)

**HMS _Sharpshooter_** was a [_Halcyon_-class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halcyon-class_minesweeper "Halcyon-class minesweeper")[minesweeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minesweeper "Minesweeper") of the British [Royal Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Navy "Royal Navy"). Built at [Devonport Dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMNB_Devonport "HMNB Devonport"), _Sharpshooter_ was completed in 1937. She served through the [Second World War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War "Second World War"), acting both in her designed role as minesweeper and as a convoy escort, escorting several [Arctic convoys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arctic_convoy "Arctic convoy"). She took part in the [evacuation from Dunkirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evacuation_from_Dunkirk "Evacuation from Dunkirk") in 1940, and sank the [German submarine _U-655_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-655 "German submarine U-655") in 1942.

Post war, she was converted to a [survey ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Survey_ship "Survey ship"), and was renamed **HMS _Shackleton_** in 1953. She was laid up into reserve in 1961 and sold for scrap in 1965.

## Design

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Design")]

The _Halcyon_ class were a class of dedicated [minesweepers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minesweeper "Minesweeper"), designed to be smaller and cheaper than the dual-purpose (minesweeping and colonial patrol vessel) minesweeping [sloops](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sloop-of-war "Sloop-of-war") that had been built since the late 1920s (i.e. the [_Bridgewater_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgewater-class_sloop "Bridgewater-class sloop"), [_Hastings_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hastings-class_sloop "Hastings-class sloop") and [_Shoreham_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoreham-class_sloop "Shoreham-class sloop")), which as their design evolved, were becoming increasingly focused on escort duties and becoming too large for use as minesweepers.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-sloops_p13-2)

_Sharpshooter_ was 245 feet 6 inches (74.83 m)[long overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Length_overall "Length overall") and 230 feet 0 inches (70.10 m)[between perpendiculars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Length_between_perpendiculars "Length between perpendiculars"), with a [beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beam_(nautical) "Beam (nautical)") of 33 feet 6 inches (10.21 m) and a [draught](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_(hull) "Draft (hull)") of 10 feet 3 inches (3.12 m) at deep load.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4)[Displacement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Displacement_(ship) "Displacement (ship)") was 835 long tons (848 t) standard[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4) and 1,330 long tons (1,350 t) deep load.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3) Two [Admiralty 3-drum water-tube boilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-drum_boiler#Admiralty_boiler "Three-drum boiler") supplied steam to geared [steam turbines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_turbine "Steam turbine") driving two shafts. The machinery was rated at 1,750 [shaft horsepower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsepower#Shaft_horsepower "Horsepower") (1,300 kW) giving a speed of 17 [knots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knot_(unit) "Knot (unit)") (20 mph; 31 km/h).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3)

Armament consisted of two [QF 4 inch (102 mm) Mk V guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QF_4_inch_Mk_V_naval_gun "QF 4 inch Mk V naval gun") on High-Angle mounts and so capable of being used for [anti-aircraft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-aircraft_warfare "Anti-aircraft warfare") duties,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3) with a close-in armament of one quadruple [Vickers .50 machine gun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vickers_.50_machine_gun "Vickers .50 machine gun") mount.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4) One of the 4-inch guns was removed during the Second World War, while the multiple machine guns were replaced by 4–8 [Oerlikon 20 mm cannon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oerlikon_20_mm_cannon "Oerlikon 20 mm cannon"). Up to 40 [depth charges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depth_charge "Depth charge") could be carried when used in the escort role.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-4-5) The ship had a crew of 80 officers and other ranks.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-conways22p63-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4)

## Construction

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Construction")]

_Sharpshooter_ was ordered on 2 March 1936 under the 1935 shipbuilding programme and was [laid down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keel_laying "Keel laying") at [Devonport Naval Dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMNB_Devonport "HMNB Devonport") on 8 June 1936.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_sharp-7) She was [launched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceremonial_ship_launching "Ceremonial ship launching") on 10 December 1936 and completed on 17 December 1937.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-jfs62p281-8)

## Service

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Service")]

Following commissioning (where she received the [pennant number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennant_number "Pennant number") N68[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-lenp201%E2%80%932-4) - this was changed to J68 in 1940[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-9)) _Sharpshooter_ joined the 1st Minesweeping Flotilla based at [Portland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_harbour "Portland harbour"). Along with the rest of her Flotilla, _Sharpshooter_ moved to [Scapa Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scapa_Flow "Scapa Flow"), the Flotilla's war station, from August to September 1938 during the [Munich crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich_crisis "Munich crisis").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6) With other ships of the flotilla she took part in the search in June 1939 for the submarine [Thetis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Thetis_(N25) "HMS Thetis (N25)") which had sunk in Liverpool Bay. She then operated with the flotilla in the Channel, and took part in the Royal Inspection (Reserve Fleet Review) at Portland on 9 August 1939.

### Second World War

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Second World War")]

_Sharpshooter_ was still a member of the 1st Minesweeping Flotilla in September 1939, at the outbreak of the Second World War.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-10)

The outbreak of war saw _Sharpshooter_ clearing channels through minefields around Scapa Flow and off [Loch Ewe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loch_Ewe "Loch Ewe") and the [Clyde estuary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clyde_estuary "Clyde estuary").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1939-11) At the end of May 1940, the [British Expeditionary Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Expeditionary_Force_(World_War_II) "British Expeditionary Force (World War II)") (BEF) was trapped by German forces at [Dunkirk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunkirk "Dunkirk"), France and it was decided to launch [Operation Dynamo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Dynamo "Operation Dynamo"), the evacuation of the BEF from Dunkirk. _Sharpshooter_ was one of the ships assigned to the evacuation.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-Rowp21-12) She made her first evacuation run on the morning of 29 May, landing 69 troops picked up from the Dunkirk beaches at [Dover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dover "Dover"), with a second run made on the morning of the 30 May, picking up 273 troops.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-BEFp98-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1940-14)_Sharpshooter_ was outbound on another run when at 22:10 hr, she collided with the Dover-bound steamer [_St Helier_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TSS_St_Helier "TSS St Helier"). _Sharpshooter_'s [bow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bow_(watercraft) "Bow (watercraft)") was badly damaged, and she was towed back to Dover by the [tugboat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tugboat "Tugboat")_Foremost 22_, the journey taking 11 hours.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-BEFp21,5-15) She was under repair at [Sheerness dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheerness_dockyard "Sheerness dockyard") and [Leith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leith "Leith") until September 1940, the opportunity being taken to fit _Sharpshooter_ with equipment for sweeping magnetic mines.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1940-14)

On 20 February 1941 _Sharpshooter_ was approaching [Harwich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harwich "Harwich") with sister ships [_Bramble_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Bramble_(J11) "HMS Bramble (J11)"), [_Britomart_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Britomart_(J22) "HMS Britomart (J22)"), [_Seagull_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Seagull_(J85) "HMS Seagull (J85)") and [_Speedy_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Speedy_(J17) "HMS Speedy (J17)") when they came under attack by two German aircraft. _Bramble_ was hit by a German bomb that failed to explode, but damage was minimal.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-damp300-16) From April, _Sharpshooter_ began to be used to escort convoys in the [Western Approaches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Approaches "Western Approaches").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1941-17)

#### Arctic convoys

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Arctic convoys")]

On 27 November 1941 she set out from [Hvalfjord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hvalfjord "Hvalfjord") in [Iceland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iceland "Iceland") as part of the escort of the [Arctic convoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arctic_convoys_of_World_War_II "Arctic convoys of World War II")[PQ 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_5 "Convoy PQ 5") to [Archangel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkhangelsk "Arkhangelsk") in the Soviet Union.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-rugp23-18)_Sharpshooter_ remained in Russia, minesweeping and providing local escort for Arctic convoys as they arrived and left Russian ports.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6) Convoys escorted included [PQ 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_8 "Convoy PQ 8"), [PQ 9/10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_9/10 "Convoy PQ 9/10"), [QP 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_QP_7 "Convoy QP 7") and [QP 9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_QP_9 "Convoy QP 9").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-rug_p25-7,_30-1-19) On the night of 17/18 January 1942, _Sharpshooter_ had just joined the escort of PQ 8 when the German submarine [_U-454_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-454 "German submarine U-454") torpedoed and sank the destroyer [_Matabele_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Matabele "HMS Matabele"). _Sharpshooter_ helped to rescue survivors from _Matebele_ then launched a counterattack against the submarine.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1942-20)

At about 8.25 pm on the evening of 24 March 1942[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-21) while escorting QP 9 [[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBuschR%C3%B6ll199945%E2%80%9346-22) the leading gunner on the forward four-inch gun of _Sharpshooter_ spotted [German submarine U-655](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-655 "German submarine U-655") on the surface beam on, about two to three cables (370 to 556 meters) away and about 10 degrees off the minesweeper's starboard bow, with no crew apparently manning the conning tower or deck. Upon being called by the officer of the watch the captain Lieutenant-Commander David Lampen immediately called for emergency full ahead and called 'Stand by to ram'. ‘’Sharpsweeper’’ had just begun to gather speed when she struck the submarine just behind the conning tower.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-Paterson-23) The submarine turned rolled over due to the impact and bumped along the minesweeper's port side sinking as it disappeared astern and sank stern first south-east of Bear Island, in approximate position 73.00N, 21.00E.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-24) No trace of the submarine or her crew of 45 was found except for two lifebuoys and what may have been a canvas dinghy.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-Paterson-23) The bow of _Sharpshooter_ was badly damaged by the collusion. After shoring up the forward mess deck, she continued at slow speed to Iceland independent of the convoy, and from there to Leith for repair.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1942-20)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-blairp549-25) She was under repair until June 1942.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)

In September 1942, _Sharpshooter_ formed part of the close escort for the Arctic convoy [PQ 18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_PQ_18 "Convoy PQ 18"), with _Sharpshooter_ being used as a rescue ship to pick survivors from sunken ships as well as for more conventional escort duties.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-rugp42-44-26)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1942-20) The convoy came under heavy air and submarine attack, with 13 ships in total being sunk. _Sharpshooter_ rescued 101 survivors during the operation.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-Rowp163-27) In November 1942, _Sharpshooter_ escorted the return convoy [QP 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy_QP_15 "Convoy QP 15") to Iceland, but on 27 November, shortly after leaving the convoy, collided with the cargo ship _Empire Snow_, badly damaging the minesweeper.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-rugp46-7-28)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1942-20)

#### Mediterranean

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Mediterranean")]

In April 1943 _Sharpshooter_ was ordered to join the 12th Minesweeping Squadron in the Mediterranean, and in July the year took part in [Operation Husky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Husky "Operation Husky"), the Allied invasion of [Sicily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sicily "Sicily").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1943-29) After Husky, _Sharpshooter_ continued to carry out minesweeping and convoy escort operations in the Mediterranean until October 1944 when she returned to home waters.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-hal_1944-30)

### Survey ship

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Survey ship")]

In May 1945, _Sharpshooter_ began conversion to a survey ship at [Chatham Dockyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chatham_Dockyard "Chatham Dockyard"). Her armament was removed during this conversion, which continued until March 1946. On 3 April 1946, _Sharpshooter_ was damaged in a collision with the merchant ship MV _Fealtie_. After repair and working up, she was deployed to [Singapore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore "Singapore"), carrying out survey operations off [Malaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malay_Peninsula "Malay Peninsula") and [Borneo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borneo "Borneo").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-post-32) During surveys of [Penang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penang "Penang"), she discovered five submerged wrecks.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-33) On 13 October 1947 she collided with the merchant ship MV _Celebes_ and after repair continued survey duties before returning to Britain at the start of 1948. After refit she recommissioned, receiving the new pennant number A310, and operating out of [Lowestoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lowestoft "Lowestoft").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31)

On 15 June 1953 she took part in the Coronation [Fleet Review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fleet_Review "Fleet Review") at [Spithead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spithead "Spithead"), and on 1 July that year was renamed _Shackleton_.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-post-32)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31) She ran aground in the [Bristol Channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol_Channel "Bristol Channel") on 28 October 1958, damaging her sonar dome.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31) On 20 August 1959, the prototype [Handley Page Victor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handley_Page_Victor "Handley Page Victor") B2 bomber crashed into the [Irish Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Sea "Irish Sea"). A large scale salvage effort was launched by the Royal Navy to locate and recover the wreckage, so the cause of the accident could be determined.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-34)_Shackleton_ was diverted from her normal survey duties to take part in this search and salvage operation,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6) and on 20 April, while searching for debris of the bomber, was diverted to the aid of a trawler, the _Starbank_, that had an uncontrolled leak. _Shackleton_ transferred pumps over to the trawler, which allowed the leak to be controlled, and escorted _Starbank_ to [Milford Haven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milford_Haven "Milford Haven").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-35)

### Disposal

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Disposal")]

_Sharpshooter_ was refitted at Devonport in 1961, but was then immediately paid off into reserve. She was placed on the disposal list in 1965 and was sold to the [British Iron & Steel Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Iron_&_Steel_Corporation "British Iron & Steel Corporation") (BISCO) for scrapping. The ship was allocated to the West of Scotland Shipbreaking Company, and arrived at their [Troon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troon "Troon") yard for breaking up on 3 November 1965.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-mason-6)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(J68)#cite_note-worthp11-31)

### **24th of March, 1942. The Atlanic**

"Emergency full ahead, stand by to ram"

~Captain David Lampen, abord the minesweeper HMS Sharpshooter~

At about 8.25 pm on the evening of 24 March 1942 while escorting QP 9 the leading gunner on the forward four-inch gun of Sharpshooter spotted German submarine U-655 on the surface beam on, about two to three cables (370 to 556 meters) away and about 10 degrees off the minesweeper's starboard bow, with no crew apparently manning the conning tower or deck. Upon being called by the officer of the watch the captain Lieutenant-Commander David Lampen immediately called for emergency full ahead and called 'Stand by to ram'. HMS Sharpshooter had just begun to gather speed when she struck the submarine just behind the conning tower. The submarine turned rolled over due to the impact and bumped along the minesweeper's port side sinking as it disappeared astern and sank stern first south-east of Bear Island. No trace of the submarine or her crew of 45 was found except for two lifebuoys and what may have been a canvas dinghy. The bow of Sharpshooter was badly damaged by the collusion. After shoring up the forward mess deck, she continued at slow speed to Iceland independent of the convoy, and from there to Leith for repair. She was under repair until June 1942.

HMS Sharpshooter was a Halcyon-class minesweeper of the British Royal Navy. Built at Devonport Dockyard, Sharpshooter was completed in 1937. She served through the Second World War, acting both in her designed role as minesweeper and as a convoy escort, escorting several Arctic convoys.

HMS Sharpshooter survived the war and in May 1945 she was converted to a survey ship, having her armament was removed during this conversion. She served in this role until she was put in reserve in 1961. She was placed on the disposal list in 1965 and was sold for scrapping.

May Channel area minesweeping with Flotilla including coastal shipping routes off Holland. April Flotilla duties in Channel and North Sea in continuation. to July (Note: Some ships of Flotilla were transferred to Western Approaches Command during this period and deployed in NW Approaches for Local Escort of Atlantic convoys) August Nominated for refit and took passage to Cardiff for repair in commercial shipyard. 6th Taken in hand for refit prior to service in North Russia. September Under refit to October (Note: It is most unlikely that the ship was “Arcticised” for service in North Russia during this refit.) (Note: For details of all Russian Convoy operations with names of the mercantiles and the escorts see CONVOYS TO RUSSIA by RA Ruegg, THE RUSSIAN CONVOYS by B Schoefield, CONVOY ! by P Kemp and ARCTIC CONVOYS by R Woodman.) 27th Sailed from Hvalfjord as escort for PQ5 with HMS HAZARD and HMS HEBE during passage to Archangel. December 7th Remained with PQ5 when HMS BRAMBLE and HMS SEAGULL joined to relieve HMS HAZARD and HMS HEBE. (Note: HM Cruiser SHEFFIELD which had joined convoy on 1st December also detached with the two minesweepers and took independent passage to Murmansk.) 13th Detached from PQ5 on arrival at Archangel without enemy interference. 14th Deployed for service in North Russia to provide Local Escort of convoys and for minesweeping to ensure clear passage for convoys on entry and departure. 1 9 4 2 January North Russia deployment in continuation 16th Provided Local Escort for Russian convoy PQ8 into Murmansk with HMS HAZARD. 17th Detached from PQ8 on arrival at Murmansk. (Note: HMS MATABELE, one of the Ocean Escort was torpedoed and sunk with heavy loss of life before arrival. See references.) February 13th Joined return convoy QP7 with HMS BRITOMART to relieve HMS HAZARD and HMS SPEEDWELL as Local Escort during part of initial stage of passage to Seidisfjord, Iceland. 15th Detached from QP8 with HMS BRITOMART and returned to Murmansk. (Note: Ocean Escort was provided by HM Destroyers FAULKNOR and INTREPID covered by HM Cruiser NIGERIA.) March 1st Deployed with HMS HARRIER, Russian destroyers GREMYASCHI and GROMKI as Local Escort for return convoy QP8 for passage from Murmansk. 3rd Detached with HMS HARRIER and took passage back to base. (Note: Ocean Escort was provided by HMS HAZARD and HMS SALAMANDER, HM Corvettes OXLIP and SWEETBRIAR covered by HMS NIGERIA and units of Home Fleet deployed to counter threat of attack by German battleship TIRPITZ on this convoy and inward PQ12. See references.) 21st Deployed with HM Destroyer OFFA and HMS BRITOMART as Ocean Escort for convoy QP9 during passage to Iceland from Kola Inlet covered by Home Fleet Fleet units. (Note: HM Cruiser KENYA intended to join on 22n February and carrying gold bullion from Russia to UK did not meet the convoy as part of Ocean Escort.) Local Escort was provided by HM Minesweepers GOSSAMER, HARRIER, HUSSAR, NIGER, SPEEDWELL and Russian destroyer GREMYASCHI.) 24th Sighted U655 on surfaced and carried out ramming attack. Submarine turned over and sank without survivors. See HITLER’S U – BOAT WAR by C Blair and above references. Sustained serious damage to forward structure. 24th Remained with QP9 as part of escort. April 3rd Detached from QP9 on arrival and Reykjavik and took passage to UK 14th Taken in hand for repair at Leith. May Under repair June 11th Resumed operational service on completion of post refit trials and work-up. July Deployed in Home waters August Nominated for escort of Russian convoy PQ18 during passage to Murmansk and further detached service in North Russia. (Note: See above references for details of the arrangements made for this transit and provision of additional escorts.) September Joined HM Destroyers ACHATES, MALCOLM, HM Auxiliary AA Ships ALYNBANK and ULSTER QUEEN, HM Corvettes BERGAMOT, BLUEBELL, BRYONY, CAMELLIA and HM Minesweeper SHARPSHOOTER for service as Close Escort for PQ18. Passage to join PQ18. 7th Joined convoy and commenced service as Close Escort. (Note: Air Cover was provided by HM Escort Aircraft Carrier AVENGER screened by HM Destroyers WHEATLAND and WILTON with a Fighting Escort comprising HM Cruiser SCYLLA and 16 destroyers from Home Fleet. HM Destroyers MONTROSE and WALPOLE had joined PQ18 escort on 6th September. HM Submarines P614 and P615 were also deployed for defence of this convoy and cruiser cover by HM Cruisers LONDON, NORFOLK and SUFFOLK. Home Fleet major warships provided Distant Cover.) 12th Under submarine attacks during which two mercantiles were sunk. 13th Under air attacks during which six of the mercantiles were sunk. 14th Under submarine attacks by U457 which hit a mercantile, later abandoned and sunk.. Air attacks in continuation during which another mercantile was sunk (For details see references.) 21st Detached from PQ18 on arrival at Archangel and commenced local duties in North Russia. October North Russia Local Minesweeping operations in continuation with detached minesweepers. November 16th Deployed with HMS HALCYON and HAZARD for minesweeping operations to ensure safe passage of local convoys. (Note: The operation was completed successfully despite gale conditions and thick fog.) 17th Deployed with HMS BRITOMART, HALCYON and HAZARD as Eastern Local Escort for return convoy QP15. 20th Detached from QP15 and took independent eastward passage. (Note: This ship is not recorded as part of Ocean Escort which did include HMS SALAMANDER and further research is required.) 27th Sustained major structural damage in collision south of Iceland. December Under temporary repair in Iceland (To be confirmed) Repair arranged at Hull in commercial shipyard. Passage to Hull 23rd Taken in hand for repair in Hull 1 9 4 3 January Under repair. February On completion of post repair trials worked up for operational minesweeping service March Deployed in Home waters for minesweeping duties. April Nominated for foreign service with 12 Minesweeping Flotilla. Passage to Mediterranean as part of escort for military convoy KMS14. May Joined Flotilla in Mediterranean and deployed for minesweeping off North African coast to ensure safe passage for convoys between Gibraltar and ports in Algeria and Tunisia. June North African coastal duties in continuation. Nominated for minesweeping support of planned landings in Sicily (Operation HUSKY). July Preparation for Sicily landings 9th Passage to Sicily with Assault Convoys 10th Deployed with HMS HEBE and HAZARD for mine sweeping in BARK WEST beach head area prior to landings, 11th Remained in landings area for convoy escort and patrol until 16th 17th Took passage to Malta on release from HUSKY August Deployed in central Mediterranean for minesweeping operations and convoy escort. to December (Note: This period included defence of convoys to Adriatic.) 1 9 4 4 January Central Mediterranean deployment in continuation. 5th Sustained structural damage after collision with HM Auxiliary LAURANA. (Note: This vessel was a captured Italian prize used as a patrol vessel..) Remained in operational use. February Transferred to 49th Escort Group and deployed in Eastern Mediterranean for to April convoy defence based at Alexandria April 5th Damaged by explosion of GNAT torpedo. (Note: No details of this incident can be traced. It is not recorded in any record of U-Boat attacks. To be investigated.) May 10th Taken in hand for repair in Haifa. June 16th On completion of repair and refit resumed duties with Group. July Convoy defence with Group in continuation. Nominated for return to UK. August Joined military convoy MKS 42 and took passage from Alexandria to UK as part of escort. September Detached from MKS 42 on arrival in UK and joined 1st Minesweeping Squadron for minesweeping operations in English Channel. (Note: Flotilla also comprised HM Minesweepers HARRIER, HALCYON, SPEEDWELL, GLEANER, HAZARD, JASON and SEAGULL. (Note: During this period extensive minelaying was being carried out by aircraft, submersibles and coastal warships, mainly to disrupt military convoys to French and Belgian ports.) April Nominated for post war deployment as a Survey Vessel. On release from operations to be Paid-off and de-stored prior to conversion. S u m m a r y o f P o s t W a r S e r v i c e May Released from Flotilla and Paid-off at Chatham. De-stored 15th Taken in hand for conversion to Survey Vessel by HM Dockyard, Chatham. May Resumed work-up in Home waters June Nominated for survey in Far East and took passage to Singapore. July Deployed for Hydrographic duties based at Singapore on arrival. to December 1 9 4 7 January Far East survey in continuation. to September October 13th Sustained damage in collision with mv CELEBES during survey work, Taken in hand for repair. November Resumed survey work. to December 1 9 4 8 January On release from duty took passage from Singapore to re-commission. to March April Paid off and under refit prior to resuming survey duties. to May June Re-commissioned for service in Homed Waters for Hydrographic deployment to July Pennant Number for visual signalling purposes changed to A310. August Deployed for survey duties in Home waters to December 1 9 4 9 t o 1 9 5 2 Home Waters survey duties in continuation (Note: Based at Lowestoft during this period for North Sea surveys.) Re-commissioned for further Home waters deployment 1 9 5 3 January Under repair by HM Dockyard, Chatham to February March Home Waters survey duty in continuation to May (Note: Carried out surveys of west coast of UK) June To be renamed **HMS SHACKLETON** Attendance at Coronation Review to be confirmed. July Re-commissioned as HMS SHACKLETON in continuation of Home Waters deployment. August Home waters deployment in continuation to December 1 9 5 4 t o 1 9 5 7 Deployed for surveying duties in western Home waters coastal areas 1 9 5 8 January West coast UK deployment in continuation. to September October 28th Grounded during survey in Bristol Channel. November Resumed survey work in Bristol Channel after replacement of to December ASDIC Dome 1 9 5 9 January West coast UK survey work in continuation. to July August Diverted from survey work to carry out search for an RAF VICTOR Bomber aircraft which crashed in the Bristol Channel. (Note: 25 square miles of the area were search and when the wreckage was located the site was combed by 11 trawlers charted by the Government in order to recover parts. Over 70% were found and sent to the Royal Aircraft Establishment at Farnborough for examination.) September Resumed survey work in Irish Sea. to December 1 9 6 0 Completion of survey in Irish Sea and Bristol Channel. Nominated for refit prior to reduction to Reserve Status. (Note: New Survey Ships had been built with latest electronic equipment designed for Hydrographic work.) 1 9 6 1 January Under refit by HM Dockyard, Devonport, To August September Carried out post refit trials prior to reduction to Reserve. to October November Completed de-storing and removal of special equipment. 9th Accepted into Reserve Fleet and laid-up at Devonport. F i n a l P h a s e HMS SHACKLETON laid-up at Devonport until placed on the Disposal List in 1965. The ship was sold to BISCO on 3rd November 1965 for breaking-up at Troon by the West of Scotland Shipbreaking Co. Ltd. On 20th November that year she arrived in tow at the breakers yard to terminate her 28 years of naval service as a minesweeper during WW2 and as Survey Ship in peace-time. * * * **Addendum** **Link to**[www.halcyon-class.co.uk](http://www.halcyon-class.co.uk/) by Bill Burn

# HMS _Sharpshooter_ (1805)

[](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#articleComments)[Sign In to Save Save](https://auth.fandom.com/register?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fmilitary-history.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FHMS_Sharpshooter_%281805%29%3Fcollections%3Dsave&uselang=en&metadata=collections-save-button "Sign In to Save")[Edit](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fmilitary-history.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FHMS_Sharpshooter_%281805%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article)

For other ships of the same name, see [HMS Sharpshooter](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter "HMS Sharpshooter").

**HMS _Sharpshooter_** (or _**Sharp Shooter**_) was launched in 1805. She operated in the Channel, often from the Channel Islands. She participated in two actions and captured a small number of merchant vessels. She was sold and broken up in 1816.

## Career[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fmilitary-history.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FHMS_Sharpshooter_%281805%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D1&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

Lieutenant John Goldie commissioned _Sharpshooter_ in April 1805.

In April 1806 _Sharp Shooter_ detained the American vessel _Commerce_, Ford, master, from Baltimore and sent her into Plymouth.[[2]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-2)

In May _Sharp Shooter_ sent _Vrienchap_, Heijelts, master, from Bordeaux, into Plymouth.[[3]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-3)

On 12 September the [post ship](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Post_ship "Post ship") HMS _Constance_ and the brigs _Sharpshooter_ and _Strenuous_ were off Saint-Malo when they sighted a French frigate of some 30 guns. They gave chase until their quarry ran aground near Cape Fréhel. The British were not able to get close enough to fire on her and the presence of French shore batteries and the French army made it too hazardous to send in their boats to cut her out.[[4]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-4)

On 29 December _General Perpignon_ [sic] captured _Patent_, Barugh, master, at [49°48′N 8°30′W / 49.8°N 8.5°W / 49.8; -8.5](http://tools.wmflabs.org/geohack/geohack.php?pagename=HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)&params=49_48_N_8_30_W_) as _Patent_ was on her way from New Providence to London. However _Sharp Shooter_ and the hired armed[cutter](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Cutter_(ship) "Cutter (ship)")_Britannia_ recaptured _Patent_ and sent her into Plymouth.[[5]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-5)

In May 1807 _Sharp Shooter_ detained _Maria_, which had been sailing from Leghorn to Tonningen, and sent her into Portsmouth.[[6]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-6)

On 11 October 1807, the French privateer _Prince Jerome_ captured the American vessel _Honeflus_, Ford, master, which had been sailing from Virginia to London. _Sharp Shooter_ recaptured _Honeflus_ and sent her into Guernsey.[[7]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-7)[[lower-alpha 1]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-9)

_Sharp Shooter_ recaptured the American ship _Honeflus_.[[9]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-10)

On 20 April 1810 the boats of [HMS _Firm_](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Firm_(1804) "HMS Firm (1804)"), [_Surly_](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Surly_(1806) "HMS Surly (1806)"), and _Sharpshooter_[cut out](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Boarding_(attack) "Boarding (attack)") the French [privateer](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Privateer "Privateer") cutter _Alcide_ from the mouth of the Pirou River, where she had taken refuge after the British vessels had chased her. _Alcide_ was moored under the protection of 400 troops on shore, who kept up an incessant fire while the boarding party carried her. _Alcide_ had thrown her four 4-pounder guns overboard during the chase to lighten her. One man was killed and another wounded, both from _Firm_.[[10]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-11) In 1847 the Admiralty awarded the Naval General Service Medal with the clasps "Firm 24 April 1810" and "Surly 24 April 1810", to all survivors of the action from those two vessels.[[lower-alpha 2]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-13)

On 5 August 1812 the Royal Navy detained _Asia_. _Sharpshooter_ was one of the many vessels that shared in the proceeds of the sale of _Asia_.[[lower-alpha 3]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-15)

On 22 November 1813 _Sharpshooter_ recaptured the Swedish brig _Mercurius_.[[13]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-16) On 20 November a French privateer from Saint-Malo captured the Swedish vessel _Mercury_, Starre, master, which was sailing from Cadiz to Gothenburg. _Sharpshooter_ recaptured _Mercury_ off Portland and she arrived at Guernsey on 23 November.[[14]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-17)

## Fate[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fmilitary-history.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FHMS_Sharpshooter_%281805%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D2&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

In September 1815 _Sharpshooter_ was paid off into [ordinary](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Reserve_fleet "Reserve fleet").[[1]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWinfield2008342-1) The "Principal Officers and Commissioners of His Majesty's Navy" offered "Sharpshooter gun-brig, of 178 tons", lying at Woolwich, for sale on 30 May 1816.[[15]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-18) She sold on that date for £600 for breaking up.[[1]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWinfield2008342-1)

**HMS _Sharpshooter_** (or _**Sharp Shooter**_) was launched in 1805. She operated in the Channel, often from the Channel Islands. She participated in two actions and captured a small number of merchant vessels. She was sold and broken up in 1816.

## Career[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fmilitary-history.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FHMS_Sharpshooter_%281805%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D1&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

Lieutenant John Goldie commissioned _Sharpshooter_ in April 1805.

In April 1806 _Sharp Shooter_ detained the American vessel _Commerce_, Ford, master, from Baltimore and sent her into Plymouth.[[2]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-2)

In May _Sharp Shooter_ sent _Vrienchap_, Heijelts, master, from Bordeaux, into Plymouth.[[3]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-3)

On 12 September the [post ship](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Post_ship "Post ship") HMS _Constance_ and the brigs _Sharpshooter_ and _Strenuous_ were off Saint-Malo when they sighted a French frigate of some 30 guns. They gave chase until their quarry ran aground near Cape Fréhel. The British were not able to get close enough to fire on her and the presence of French shore batteries and the French army made it too hazardous to send in their boats to cut her out.[[4]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-4)

On 29 December _General Perpignon_ [sic] captured _Patent_, Barugh, master, at [49°48′N 8°30′W / 49.8°N 8.5°W / 49.8; -8.5](http://tools.wmflabs.org/geohack/geohack.php?pagename=HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)&params=49_48_N_8_30_W_) as _Patent_ was on her way from New Providence to London. However _Sharp Shooter_ and the hired armed[cutter](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Cutter_(ship) "Cutter (ship)")_Britannia_ recaptured _Patent_ and sent her into Plymouth.[[5]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-5)

In May 1807 _Sharp Shooter_ detained _Maria_, which had been sailing from Leghorn to Tonningen, and sent her into Portsmouth.[[6]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-6)

On 11 October 1807, the French privateer _Prince Jerome_ captured the American vessel _Honeflus_, Ford, master, which had been sailing from Virginia to London. _Sharp Shooter_ recaptured _Honeflus_ and sent her into Guernsey.[[7]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-7)[[lower-alpha 1]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-9)

_Sharp Shooter_ recaptured the American ship _Honeflus_.[[9]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-10)

On 20 April 1810 the boats of [HMS _Firm_](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Firm_(1804) "HMS Firm (1804)"), [_Surly_](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Surly_(1806) "HMS Surly (1806)"), and _Sharpshooter_[cut out](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Boarding_(attack) "Boarding (attack)") the French [privateer](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Privateer "Privateer") cutter _Alcide_ from the mouth of the Pirou River, where she had taken refuge after the British vessels had chased her. _Alcide_ was moored under the protection of 400 troops on shore, who kept up an incessant fire while the boarding party carried her. _Alcide_ had thrown her four 4-pounder guns overboard during the chase to lighten her. One man was killed and another wounded, both from _Firm_.[[10]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-11) In 1847 the Admiralty awarded the Naval General Service Medal with the clasps "Firm 24 April 1810" and "Surly 24 April 1810", to all survivors of the action from those two vessels.[[lower-alpha 2]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-13)

On 5 August 1812 the Royal Navy detained _Asia_. _Sharpshooter_ was one of the many vessels that shared in the proceeds of the sale of _Asia_.[[lower-alpha 3]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-15)

On 22 November 1813 _Sharpshooter_ recaptured the Swedish brig _Mercurius_.[[13]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-16) On 20 November a French privateer from Saint-Malo captured the Swedish vessel _Mercury_, Starre, master, which was sailing from Cadiz to Gothenburg. _Sharpshooter_ recaptured _Mercury_ off Portland and she arrived at Guernsey on 23 November.[[14]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-17)

## Fate[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fmilitary-history.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FHMS_Sharpshooter_%281805%29%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D2&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")]

In September 1815 _Sharpshooter_ was paid off into [ordinary](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/Reserve_fleet "Reserve fleet").[[1]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWinfield2008342-1) The "Principal Officers and Commissioners of His Majesty's Navy" offered "Sharpshooter gun-brig, of 178 tons", lying at Woolwich, for sale on 30 May 1816.[[15]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-18) She sold on that date for £600 for breaking up.[[1]](https://military-history.fandom.com/wiki/HMS_Sharpshooter_(1805)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWinfield2008342-1)

[![Image 1](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/hms_sharpshooter_1938_iwm_fl_18955.jpg?resize=800%2C530&ssl=1)](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/?attachment_id=55513)
_Photograph FL 18955 from the collections of the Imperial War Museums_

Here we see the Royal Navy _Halcyon_-class “sloop minesweeper” _HMS Sharpshooter (N68/J68)_in September 1938, at around the time Hitler sent troops into the Sudetenland and a year before he was to send them into Poland, sparking WWII. Not a very imposing ship, some 80 years ago this week she would single-handedly send a Jerry U-boat to the bottom of the Barents Sea.

Based on the _Grimsby_-class sloops-of-war– a baker’s dozen 1,500-ton, 266-foot slow-moving (16 knots) sub chasers built in the early 1930s and capable of hauling almost 100 depth charges along with some light guns– the 21-unit _Halcyon_-class were slightly smaller, running 245-feet overall, and logically lighter at 1,400-tons. Outfitted with two QF MK V 4″/45 singles and a smattering of machine guns (both .50 cal Vickers and .303 Lewis guns), they shipped with manual sweep gear rather than ASW equipment.

[![Image 2](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/halycon-players-card-tile.jpg?resize=860%2C447&ssl=1)](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/?attachment_id=55515)

The first five _Halcyons_ (ordered 1933-35) were fitted with forced lubricating compound engines, and the next two with reciprocating steam (VTE) engines, while the latter 14 (ordered 1936-37 as Europe was ramping up for war) used Parsons steam turbines, with all versions being able to hit at least 16.5 knot-ish while the latter upgrades able to touch 17. All were named for Great War-era destroyers or minesweepers.

Our little sweeper, _Sharpshooter_, was of the latter “turbine” type and was laid down at HM Dockyard Devonport on 8 June 1936, the fifth (and as of 2022, the last) RN warship to carry the name dating back to a 12-gun _Archer_-class gunbrig of the Napoleonic era. Commissioned 17 December 1937 with pennant N68, this later shifted to J68.

Assigned to the 1st Minesweeping Flotilla based at Portland (soon shifting to Scapa) her pre-war service included searching for the lost T-class submarine _HMS Thetis (N25)_, which sank during sea trials in Liverpool Bay in the summer of 1939.

### War!

Once the war began (see **U-boat.net**and [**Halcyon-class.co.uk**](http://www.halcyon-class.co.uk/sharpshooter/sharpshooter_1940.htm) for an extensive chronicle of her WWII service) _Sharpshooter_ worked mine sweeping assignments in the North Sea and off Scotland, then in November transferred to Stornoway for Atlantic convoy escort duties with her Flotilla, then transferred to the 6th MS Flotilla in April 1940.

[![Image 3](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/hms-sharpshooter-halcyon-class-iwm-a.jpg?resize=860%2C503&ssl=1)](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/?attachment_id=55529)

The seven sweepers of the 6th MSF, _Sharpshooter_ included, moved to the Dover area in May, where, in response to the Blitzkrieg of the Lowlands, conducted sweeps of the coastal shipping routes off Holland. Often under German air attack on this detail, two units of the Flotilla (sisterships _Hussar_ and _Harrier_) were damaged by Luftwaffe bombs before the month was up.

Called close to the beaches of Dunkirk on 28 May to help pull off members of the BEF desperate to escape the Fall of France, _Sharpshooter_ arrived off the beaches at 0115 on 29 May and began putting boats in the water to fight the inshore surf and remove men directly from the sand—after all, she and her sisters could float in just 9-feet of water.

[![Image 4](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/dunkirk-26-29-may-1940-british-troops-line-up-on-the-beach-at-dunkirk-to-await-evacuation-iwm.jpg?resize=860%2C606&ssl=1)](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/2020/06/01/a-flag-unstained-80-years-ago-today/dunkirk-26-29-may-1940-british-troops-line-up-on-the-beach-at-dunkirk-to-await-evacuation-iwm/)
_Dunkirk 26-29 May 1940 British troops line up on the beach at Dunkirk to await evacuation IWM_

By noon on the 29th, she landed 100 soggy but safe soldiers at Dover.

On the 30th, she disembarked 273 troops at Dover, then, headed back to the beaches late that night, had a collision with the French steamer _St. Helier_ which was pulling off French troops. This forced her to be towed back to Dover sans any more Tommys, facing a repair that would put her out of the war until mid-September.

_Sharpshooter_ finished 1940 based at Scapa conducting fleet minesweeping/route clearance duties.

In January 1941, she was part of the sweeping screen to the north of Rockall for the battleship _HMS King George V_, which was taking Lord Halifax across the Atlantic to his post as the new British Ambassador at Washington.

[![Image 5](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/two-minesweepers-at-a-northern-base.-hms-sharpshooter-is-on-the-left-january-1941.-iwm-a-2702.jpg?resize=800%2C538&ssl=1)](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/?attachment_id=55517)
_LORD HALIFAX LEAVES FOR THE USA IN HMS KING GEORGE V TO TAKE UP HIS POST AS AMBASSADOR. JANUARY 1941. (A 2702) Two Minesweepers at a northern base. HMS SHARPSHOOTER is on the left. Copyright: © IWM. Original Source: [http://www.iwm.org.uk/collections/item/object/205137059](http://www.iwm.org.uk/collections/item/object/205137059)_

Following that, _Sharpshooter_ became a facet on North Atlantic convoy work, clocking on with HX 125, OB 334, PQ 8, PQ 9/10, PQ 12, PQ 13, QP 8, QP 9, PQ 18, QP 14, and QP 15 across 1941 and 1942, alternating with minesweeping operations in North Russian waters and off Allied-occupied Iceland. This duty usually consisted of riding shotgun on slow-moving Russia-bound convoys from Reykjavik to Murmansk/Archangel and back, being targets in the massive Barents Sea shooting gallery off German-occupied Norway which meant deadly threats from shore-based bombers, U-boats, and the bulk of the Kriegsmarine’s surface assets.

This brings us to _Sharpshooter’s_ encounter with the [Type VIIC submarine _U-655_](https://uboat.net/boats/u655.htm) (KrvKpt. Adolf Dumrese) of Wolfpack Ziethen. Our minesweeper, part of Convoy QP 9 on a return run from Murmansk to Reykjavik, spotted Dumrese’s surfaced U-boat at very close range on the morning of 24 March 1942 south-east of Bear Island– and promptly rammed it.

_U-655_ turned over and sank without survivors while the minesweeper suffered no losses.

This required _Sharpshooter_ to return to the dockyard for 10 weeks of repairs to her bow and post refit trials. Meanwhile, her skipper, [LCDR David Lampen](https://www.thegazette.co.uk/London/issue/35679/page/3721/data.pdf) received the DSO on 25 August “awarded for skill and coolness in successful actions against enemy submarines while serving in _HMS Sharpshooter_.”

By April 1943, _Sharpshooter_ was dispatched to the Mediterranean for minesweeping off the North African coast then, as summer went on, for the Operation Husky Sicily landings. She remained in the Med through most of 1944, where she reportedly suffered a partial (?) torpedo hit in April.

Arriving back in the UK in September 1944, she conducted sweeping off the coast of France and Belgium before switching to North Sea operations into early 1945.

### A second career

With no shortage of minesweepers and proper sloops, and the war in Europe over, the Admiralty in April 1945 made the call to disarm _Sharpshooter_ (along with her sister ships _HMS Seagull, Franklin,_ and _Scott_) then [convert them to survey ships.](http://www.halcyon-class.co.uk/sharpshooter/sharpshooter_post-war.htm)

[![Image 6](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/halcyon-class-survey-ships-1946-janes.jpg?resize=860%2C627&ssl=1)](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/?attachment_id=55525)
_The 1946 Jane’s listing for the Halcyon class survey ship conversions, including HMS Sharpshooter_

_Sharpshooter_ emerged with a white scheme in May 1946 and was soon dispatched for hydrographic duties in the shipwreck-plagued South Pacific, based in Singapore, later picking up the auxiliary pennant A310.

[![Image 7](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/hms-shackleton.jpg?resize=860%2C595&ssl=1)](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/?attachment_id=55523)

Returning to the UK in December 1948, she spent the next several years on surveys of the Home Islands’ West coast and, just in time for the 1953 Coronation Review, was renamed _HMS Shackleton_ after the famed British explorer. She and her two sisters [located and logged](https://cold-war.muninn-project.org/crowsnest/Crowsnest-1960_2.pdf) many war-time wrecks while re-surveying coastal Great Britain.

A familiar sight from Portsmouth to the Irish Sea, _Sharpshooter/Shackleton_ was reduced to reserve status in 1961 and laid up at Devonport.

On the disposal list in 1965, she was sold to BISCO on 3 November for breaking up at Troon by the West of Scotland Shipbreaking Co. Ltd.

### Epilogue

The _Halcyons_ suffered terribly during WWII. _Sphinx, Skipjack, Gossamer, Niger, Leda, Bramble, Hebe, Hussar,_ and _Britomart_ were all sunk in enemy (or blue-on-blue) action off Iceland, Dunkirk, Normandy, the Barents Sea, and in Russia’s Kola Bay– all the same waters where Sharpshooter narrowly avoided destruction herself.

As peace settled into a frigid Cold War, these slow and well-worn sweeper sloops were not needed, and most were immediately laid up.

[![Image 8](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/halcyon-class-1946-janes.jpg?resize=860%2C931&ssl=1)](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/?attachment_id=55527)
_Just four Halcyons were listed as active in the 1946 edition of Jane’s, the rest lost during the war or converted to survey ships._

The Royal Navy sold almost all of _Sharpshooter/Shackleton’s_ remaining sisters by the mid-1950s. The only outlier to this was _HMS Scott_, which had likewise been tasked with survey work, and was sold for scrap in 1965 along with _Sharpshooter_.

_Sharpshooter_, her name not since reused by the Admiralty, is at least remembered by a [Displate](https://displate.com/displate/4641194).

[![Image 9](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/hms-sharpshooter.jpg?resize=860%2C614&ssl=1)](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/?attachment_id=55519)

While Shackleton, his name recently very much in the news, gets much more attention and maritime art exists of _Sharpshooter_ in this post-war survey guise.

[![Image 10](https://i0.wp.com/laststandonzombieisland.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/hms-shackleton-painting.jpg?resize=842%2C594&ssl=1)](https://laststandonzombieisland.com/?attachment_id=55521)
